the current motion lib has duration-based transitions with cubic-bezier easing and static presets where enter and exit are mirror images of each other. this plan upgrades it to support the bloom-style animation patterns while keeping the existing api working. everything below happens in packages/duck-motion/src/.

the motion-tokens.ts file currently exports duckMotionTransition with duration+ease objects like { duration: 0.15, ease: [0.4, 0, 0.2, 1] }. it needs a new export called duckSpring that provides spring-based transitions using the visualDuration+bounce pattern from the motion library. the defaults should be duckSpring.default with visualDuration 0.25 and bounce 0.2 for general use, duckSpring.snappy with visualDuration 0.2 and bounce 0.15 for menus and popovers, duckSpring.gentle with visualDuration 0.35 and bounce 0.25 for dialogs and sheets, and duckSpring.instant which is the reduced motion fallback with stiffness 1000 and damping 100. the existing duckMotionTransition stays untouched for backwards compatibility. a new duckBlur export should provide the standard blur amounts as numbers: duckBlur.light at 4, duckBlur.medium at 8, duckBlur.heavy at 10. these are just numbers that consumers format into filter strings themselves.

the motion-presets.tsx file needs the biggest rework. the current presets have symmetric enter/exit (same values just reversed) and no blur except on scaleIn. the new presets need three things: asymmetric exit values where the exit goes further than enter, blur on enter/exit states, and direction awareness.

the preset definitions should change from the current flat structure to one where exit values differ from initial. for example scaleIn currently has initial scale 0.8 and exit scale 0.8, but it should have initial scale 0.95 and exit scale 0.9 following bloom's pattern where closing feels snappier. the blur on initial should be 8px and on exit should be 8px.

add new directional presets that take a direction parameter. a new function called createDirectionalPreset(direction, options) should return a MotionPreset where the offset direction matches the direction parameter. for direction top the content enters from y 8 and exits to y 30 (moving away from trigger). for direction bottom the content enters from y -8 and exits to y -30. for left the content enters from x 8 and exits to x 30. for right the content enters from x -8 and exits to x -30. every directional preset includes blur and scale by default.

the useMotionPreset hook interface needs to expand. the options parameter should accept direction as an optional field. when direction is provided, the preset automatically adjusts its offsets. it should also accept enterTransition and exitTransition separately so consumers can use different timing for enter vs exit (bloom uses duration 0.2 with ease [0.4, 0, 1, 1] for exit which is faster and more aggressive than the spring-based enter). a delay field should also be available for the staggered content timing pattern.

the new useMotionPreset signature should look like this: useMotionPreset(name, { direction, delay, enterTransition, exitTransition, transition }). when only transition is provided it applies to both enter and exit. when enterTransition and exitTransition are provided they override transition for their respective phases. the exit animation in the returned preset should use exitTransition when available, falling back to transition, falling back to the default spring.

add a new export called useDirectionalPreset that is a convenience wrapper specifically for menu/popover animations. it takes direction and options and returns a preset with the directional offset, blur, asymmetric scale, spring enter transition, and fast tween exit transition already configured. this is the one-liner consumers use for dropdown menus: const preset = useDirectionalPreset('bottom', { delay: 0.03 }) and spread it onto their motion.div.

the motion-provider.tsx file needs a new prop called defaultSpring that accepts a spring config object (visualDuration + bounce). when provided it replaces the duration-based duckMotionTransition.fast as the global default. this lets consumers opt their entire app into spring-based motion with one prop change on the provider.

for the test files, motion-tokens.test.ts needs new tests for duckSpring covering all four spring presets and duckBlur covering the three blur values. motion-presets.test.ts needs tests for the asymmetric exit values (exit scale 0.9 not equal to initial scale 0.95), directional presets (verify offset direction matches direction parameter), the delay option, and separate enter/exit transitions. a new test file motion-presets-directional.test.ts should cover createDirectionalPreset and useDirectionalPreset with all four directions.

the implementation order should be motion-tokens first since it has no dependencies on other new code, then motion-presets since it depends on motion-tokens, then motion-provider since it depends on both, then tests for each file after the source is written.

no changes to index.ts are needed because the new exports are in existing subpath files that already have wildcard exports in package.json. consumers import from @gentleduck/motion/motion-tokens and @gentleduck/motion/motion-presets which already resolve.

the key design decision is that the spring-based and duration-based systems coexist. nothing is removed or replaced. consumers who want the ios feel use duckSpring and useDirectionalPreset. consumers who want the simpler duration-based system keep using duckMotionTransition and the basic useMotionPreset. both work and both respect reduced motion.
